source: CARDI book "ដំណាំស្រូវនៅកម្ពុជា" (Rice Cultivation in Cambodia), by Men Sarom, Thuy Lina and Pheng Thimuny, published by CARDI, 2007. No elibrary URL visible.
text: Cambodia's modern rice research and extension system was rebuilt during the 1990s-2000s after decades of war. Under the Cambodia-IRRI-Australia Project (CIAP), a partnership involving the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) and Australian funding, a rice research station was established at Prateahlang, Kandal province (on route toward Kien Svay), starting around 1991, focused on rebuilding rice variety development and agronomic research capacity and training Cambodian researchers. This work fed into the founding of the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI) on 16 February 1999, which absorbed and continued the rice research and varietal development program (the same CARDI campus, buildings, and mandate referenced throughout the rest of this knowledge base). Since then, the described strategy for continued rice development in Cambodia has centered on four pillars: (1) developing and releasing improved rice varieties adapted to Cambodian conditions with good grain quality and disease/pest resistance suited to local growing environments; (2) irrigation policy and water-management strategy at the national level; (3) investment in postharvest infrastructure (e.g. drying, storage, milling); and (4) capacity-building of agricultural technical staff. This is background on where Cambodia's rice research institutions came from, not a farming technique in itself, but is included as context for understanding why CARDI recommendations recur throughout this knowledge base.
